get.description:
DEPRECATED. Use `/api/v2/events/{event_id}/lineups/` instead. The v2 endpoint unifies official confirmed lineups and AI-predicted lineups under a single URL with a `lineup_status` discriminator (`unavailable` | `predicted` | `confirmed`). The `beta: true` flag from v1 is replaced by `lineup_status: predicted`.

Field mapping:
- `lineups.{home,away}.team` → `lineups.{home,away}.team_name`
- `lineups.{home,away}.predicted_formation` → `lineups.{home,away}.formation`
- `confidence` (0–100) → `lineups.{home,away}.confidence` (0–1)
- `starters` → `lineups.{home,away}.players`
- `bench` → `lineups.{home,away}.substitutes`
- `404` when not generated → `200` with `lineup_status: unavailable`

This endpoint will be removed in a future release.

- `tz=…` → not supported, all datetimes returned in UTC (Z)
- Response shape changed: fields are now grouped under `markets`, `recommendations`, `model`. See `/api/v2/predictions/` docs.

- `manager=X` → `manager_id=X`
- `since=X` → `published_after=X` (ISO 8601 UTC)
- `source` field → removed (vendor name no longer exposed)
- `media_urls` → `media` (normalized: `[{type, url, width, height}]`)
- `account_handle`/`account_name`/`account_verified` → grouped under `account` object
- `teams`/`events`/`players`/`managers` arrays → grouped under `linked` object
- v2 adds detail endpoint `/api/v2/social/{id}/` and entity-scoped sub-resources (`/teams/{id}/social/`, `/events/{id}/social/`, `/players/{id}/social/`, `/managers/{id}/social/`).
- v2 adds pagination (`limit`/`offset`).
- v2 excludes `news` items — only `tweet` and `video` are returned.

This endpoint will be removed in a future release.

Returns a blended feed of three item types:
 - **tweet** — posts from official club Twitter accounts
 - **video** — YouTube match-highlight videos
 - **news** — editorial articles from third-party football news sources
Each item carries M2M links to the teams it was pulled from plus heuristic links to the current-squad players, current manager, and nearby match (±36h of publish time) for that team. Tweets refresh every 30 minutes, highlights every 6 hours, news every hour.

Only what changed about scheduled matches: a kickoff that moved, a match postponed or abandoned, a venue switch, a broadcaster added. Poll this instead of re-fetching fixture lists and diffing them yourself.

Market+outcome compatibility (incoherent combos return 400):
- 1x2            → HOME, DRAW, AWAY
- btts           → yes, no
- over_under_05/15/25/35 → over, under
- double_chance  → 1X, 12, X2
- draw_no_bet    → HOME, AWAY
- total_corners  → over, under (line in `line` field)
- corners_1x2    → HOME, DRAW, AWAY (which team has more corners)
- total_red_cards → over, under (line in `line` field)
- red_card       → yes, no (a red card is shown in the match)
- european_handicap → HOME, DRAW, AWAY (whole line in `line`, no push)
- asian_handicap → HOME, AWAY (line in `line`, settlement in `push`)

For total_corners/total_red_cards/european_handicap/asian_handicap the line varies per quote and is returned in the `line` field (null for all other markets).

Asian handicap lines are home-relative and may be quarter lines: `line=-0.25` means the home team starts a quarter goal down, and the AWAY leg of that same quote is +0.25. The `push` field carries the settlement rule the price alone cannot express — "none" on half lines, "full" on whole lines (stake returned), "half" on quarter lines (stake split, half returned).

EventIncidentsV2Schema.description:
Everything that happened in the match, in order.

**This is where the goalscorers are.** Keys vary by incident `type`, so the
array is described rather than typed field by field. A goal reads:

    {"type": "goal", "player": "M. Oyarzabal", "player_id": 4821,
     "minute": 22, "is_home": false, "assist": "D. Olmo",
     "home_score": 0, "away_score": 1}

`type` is one of exactly seven values — `goal`, `card`, `substitution`,
`period`, `injuryTime`, `varDecision`, `penalty_missed` — and nothing
else is published. Common keys: `minute`, `added_time` (only in stoppage
time), `is_home` (false = the event's away team), `home_score` /
`away_score` (the score after the incident), `text`, `is_live`.

**A penalty missed in play is a `penalty_missed`**, never a `goal`:

    {"type": "penalty_missed", "player": "A. Gouiri", "player_id": 3127,
     "minute": 59, "is_home": false, "reason": "saved"}

`reason` is `saved` (the goalkeeper saved it), `post` (it hit the
woodwork) or `miss` (off target). A scored penalty stays a `goal`, and
penalty shoot-out kicks are not incidents of the match.

**VAR decisions are here, including disallowed goals.** A `varDecision`
carries `decision`, one of:

- `goalNotAwarded` — a goal was disallowed on review. This is the one to
  filter on for chalked-off goals; the review's reason (offside, foul,
  handball) is not published, so it is not available.
- `goalAwarded` — a goal was given on review.
- `penaltyAwarded` / `penaltyNotAwarded` — a penalty given or refused.
- `cardUpgrade` — a card was upgraded, normally to red.
- `redCardGiven` — a red shown on review.
- `mistakenIdentity` — the wrong player had been sanctioned.
- `review` — an on-field review whose outcome is not published.

It also carries `confirmed`: true when the on-field decision stood, false
when the review changed it (about one in eight).

Every `*_id` — `player_id`, `player_in_id`, `player_out_id` and
`sequence[*].pid` — is our internal Player id, so it joins straight against
/api/v2/players/{id}/. A goal may carry a `sequence`: the build-up
positions leading to it.

Every bookmaker side by side for one match.

`markets` is keyed by market name (`1x2`, `over_under`, `asian_handicap`,
`btts`, `draw_no_bet`, …), and each market is keyed by an outcome code —
`HOME`, `OVER@2.5`, `AWAY@-1.75`. Codes, not team names, so a parser
survives a club being renamed. Which markets and lines appear depends on
what the bookmakers priced for this match, so both levels are open maps.

main_lines.description: market name -> the main line of that market, for the markets that have one. A match publishes eight or ten Asian handicaps and this says which of them is THE handicap for the match: the line where the two best prices sit closest together, which is the one the market treats as a coin flip. Computed from the best price on each side rather than from any one bookmaker, so the answer does not change with who you ask. Absent for markets with no line, and for a line nobody priced on both sides.

LeagueStandingsV2Schema.description:
A season's table.

Two shapes, told apart by `grouped`. A league returns a flat `standings`
array with `zones` as its legend. A competition played in groups returns
`groups` and `zones` as maps keyed by group name instead, and `standings`
is absent — so branch on `grouped` rather than assuming either key.

zones.description: The legend: which positions lead where. A list of bands when `grouped` is false, or a map of group name -> list when it is true. Each band carries `key`, `label`, `type` and the `from`/`to` positions it spans. Empty when the competition publishes no bands and none are declared.

PlayerStatV2Schema.description:
One player's line in one match.

Declared off the model rather than by hand: `serialize_player_stat` maps
every key straight onto a `PlayerEventStatistics` column, and seventy-odd
hand-copied field declarations would start drifting the first time a
counter is added. Served by both /players/{id}/stats/ and
/events/{id}/player-stats/.

A counter the provider did not send for a match comes back as 0, not null;
the nullable fields are the rated and modelled ones (`rating`,
